main.title: Rock Band 3
main.summary: Rock Band 3 is a 2010 rhythm game developed by Harmonix.

cards.text: Rock Band 3 is a 2010 rhythm game developed by Harmonix. The game was initially published and distributed by MTV Games and Electronic Arts, respectively, on October 26, 2010. Mad Catz took over both roles and re-released the title on November 23, 2011. It is the third main installment and the seventh console release in the Rock Band series. As with the previous titles, Rock Band 3 allows players to simulate the playing of rock music and many other subgenres using special instrument controllers mimicking lead and bass guitar, keyboard, drums, and vocals. Rock Band 3 expands upon previous games by including three-part vocal harmonies — previously used in The Beatles: Rock Band and Green Day: Rock Band (up to 3 singers on a song) — plus support for MIDI-compatible keyboards, electronic drumkits, and even use of a real guitar in "Pro" mode.

Pro mode introduces instrument-specific playing beyond the original button patterns. Guitar and bass parts require positions on strings and frets; drums distinguish cymbals from other pads; keyboards use notes across the instrument. Compatible controllers include a button-based guitar and an electronic Fender Squier. Players can mix Pro instruments with the original controllers in the same band.

The disc contains 83 songs, with keyboard parts broadening the repertoire. Compatible earlier downloads and Rock Band Network songs expand the library, while setlists, challenges and search tools help players organise a large collection. Support differs by instrument and track, with Pro arrangements adding another way to play suitable songs.

Rock Band 3 was initially released worldwide during the last week of October 2010 for the Xbox 360, PlayStation 3, Wii and Nintendo DS. The game received universal acclaim from critics, with praise for the addition of keyboards that broadens the potential music library for the series and the revamped career structure to keep players invested in the title. The game's Pro mode was particularly highlighted by reviewers, who stated that the mode brings the rhythm game genre to the point of teaching players to learn real instruments and have fun doing so by disguising practice into gameplay. Rock Band 3 is cited by some to be one of the greatest games of all time while also considered a pinnacle of the genre. It was also the last Rock Band game to be distributed by Electronic Arts as Mad Catz signed on to produce future Rock Band games.

main.title: Golden Sun: Dark Dawn
main.subtitle: The next generation of Adepts
main.summary: Golden Sun: Dark Dawn is Camelot's Nintendo DS role-playing adventure set thirty years after the first two Golden Sun games. Descendants of the earlier heroes travel through a changed Weyard, carrying forward the elemental powers known as Psynergy. The new generation makes the journey approachable without abandoning the series' central ideas. Turn-based battles share the adventure with environmental puzzles, and the same magic can have a practical use outside combat. Progress is measured both by a stronger party and by the places its abilities now allow it to reach.

cards.heading: The next generation of Adepts
cards.text: Golden Sun: Dark Dawn is Camelot's Nintendo DS role-playing adventure set thirty years after the first two Golden Sun games. Descendants of the earlier heroes travel through a changed Weyard, carrying forward the elemental powers known as Psynergy. The new generation makes the journey approachable without abandoning the series' central ideas. Turn-based battles share the adventure with environmental puzzles, and the same magic can have a practical use outside combat. Progress is measured both by a stronger party and by the places its abilities now allow it to reach.

cards.heading: A spell can open another route
cards.text: Psynergy is used to manipulate the environment, making a dungeon's arrangement something the party can gradually alter. New powers are gained through development or important items, and another ability can reveal a route or secret previously out of reach. The DS gives these interactions a different physical presentation from the Game Boy Advance games. The recurring question remains clear: which property of this place can an elemental skill affect? Exploration works best when the player treats a spell as a possible tool before thinking of it as another attack.

cards.heading: Collecting possibilities for the party
cards.text: Elemental Djinn augment the party's powers, connecting the search for small creatures to the way characters perform in battle. Equipment, supportive magic and offensive abilities provide further choices when the party meets monsters. An encyclopedia records returning concepts and new information, helping a newcomer follow the world that the earlier adventures established. Dark Dawn brings that world into three-dimensional environments while keeping its distinctive relationship between magic and travel. A useful discovery can improve the next fight, but it may also change the way a familiar obstacle is approached.

main.title: Solatorobo: Red the Hunter
main.subtitle: A hunter among floating islands
main.summary: Solatorobo: Red the Hunter is CyberConnect2's Nintendo DS action role-playing adventure set among floating islands inhabited by doglike Caninu and catlike Felineko. Red Savarin works as a freelance hunter with his small machine, the Dahak, until an ordinary assignment draws him into a much larger mystery. The game shares its world with Tail Concerto and features character art by Nobuteru Yuki. Illustrated people, mechanical equipment and skybound settlements give the adventure a coherent personality, making a hired job feel like a doorway into a world with an everyday life of its own.

cards.heading: A hunter among floating islands
cards.text: Solatorobo: Red the Hunter is CyberConnect2's Nintendo DS action role-playing adventure set among floating islands inhabited by doglike Caninu and catlike Felineko. Red Savarin works as a freelance hunter with his small machine, the Dahak, until an ordinary assignment draws him into a much larger mystery. The game shares its world with Tail Concerto and features character art by Nobuteru Yuki. Illustrated people, mechanical equipment and skybound settlements give the adventure a coherent personality, making a hired job feel like a doorway into a world with an everyday life of its own.

cards.heading: Pick up the problem and throw it
cards.text: The Dahak's long arms can grab objects and enemies, then throw them into another target. Repeatedly catching and tossing an opponent builds a sequence of attacks, giving combat a distinctive physical rhythm. Purchased parts fit into upgrade slots, allowing the machine to be customised as more space becomes available. Red can also climb out to swim, use ladders or operate switches. The two scales complement one another: the machine provides strength, while its pilot can enter places and perform actions that the larger body cannot manage.

cards.heading: Work earns a place in the world
cards.text: Side quests raise Red's hunter rank and open further progress, making local assignments part of the adventure's structure. A task may ask for an item, assistance to a resident or a different activity, providing reasons to visit the islands beyond the central mystery. Chikayo Fukuda's music and Madhouse's animated sequences support the story's changes in scale. Solatorobo gives its setting weight through that movement between jobs and discoveries. Red begins with practical work to complete, and the people encountered through it gradually make the wider conflict matter.

main.title: Golden Joystick Awards 2010
main.summary: The Golden Joystick Awards, with every category winner of the 2010 edition.

cards.heading: The players' awards
cards.text: The Golden Joystick Awards celebrate games through a public vote, bringing players into the choice of each year's winners. The awards began in Britain with the 1983 season and later reached an international audience through online voting. Their changing categories trace the growth of games: home computers and consoles, handhelds, online play, independent studios, performance and music. Alongside the public vote, special honours recognise individual contributions to the industry. Each edition preserves its own category names, so the results also show what players and the awards organisers considered worth celebrating at the time.

main.title: God of War: Ghost of Sparta
main.summary: God of War: Ghost of Sparta is a 2010 action-adventure game developed by Ready at Dawn and published by Sony Computer Entertainment (SCE).

cards.heading: Kratos searches for Deimos
cards.text: God of War: Ghost of Sparta is a 2010 action-adventure game developed by Ready at Dawn and published by Sony Computer Entertainment (SCE). It was first released for the PlayStation Portable (PSP) handheld console on November 2, 2010. The game is the sixth installment in the God of War series and the fifth chronologically. Loosely based on Greek mythology, Ghost of Sparta is set in ancient Greece with vengeance as its central motif. The player controls the protagonist Kratos, the God of War. Kratos is still haunted by the visions of his mortal past and decides to explore his origins. In Atlantis, he finds his mother Callisto, who claims that his brother Deimos is still alive. Kratos journeys to the Domain of Death to rescue his brother. After initial resentment from Deimos, the brothers team up to battle the God of Death, Thanatos, Deimos' captor.

cards.heading: The Blades of Athena on PSP
cards.text: The gameplay is similar to that of the previous installments, and focuses on combo-based combat, achieved through the player's main weapon—the Blades of Athena—and a secondary weapon acquired later in the game. It features quick time events that require the player to complete various game controller actions in a timed sequence to defeat stronger enemies and bosses. Up to three magical attacks and a power-enhancing ability can be used as alternative combat options. Ghost of Sparta also features puzzles and platforming elements. The combat system was updated with significantly more gameplay elements than its previous PSP installment, God of War: Chains of Olympus.

cards.heading: Reception and the remastered collection
cards.text: Ghost of Sparta received praise from critics for its story, scope, and graphical illustration, though criticism was given for the general lack of gameplay innovation from its predecessor, Chains of Olympus. By June 2012, it had sold almost 3.2 million copies worldwide, making it the nineteenth best-selling PlayStation Portable game of all time. Together with Chains of Olympus, Ghost of Sparta was remastered and released on September 13, 2011, as part of the God of War: Origins Collection and the remastered version was re-released on August 28, 2012, as part of the God of War Saga, both for the PlayStation 3.

main.title: GoldenEye 007
main.summary: Eurocom retells GoldenEye for Wii with Daniel Craig as Bond, combining updated missions with local split-screen competition.

cards.heading: Daniel Craig reimagines GoldenEye for the Wii
cards.text: Eurocom developed GoldenEye 007 for Wii, published by Activision in November 2010. It reimagines the film and Nintendo 64 game around Daniel Craig's Bond, with Judi Dench returning as M. Bruce Feirstein updated the story for a post-Cold War setting while keeping characters such as Alec Trevelyan. A separate Nintendo DS version was developed by n-Space.

cards.heading: Modern equipment meets motion controls
cards.text: The missions add destructible environments, regenerating health and a mobile phone for scanning documents, taking pictures and contacting MI6. Players can choose the Wii Remote and Nunchuk, Wii Zapper, Classic Controller variants or a GameCube controller. Motion-control users can lean around cover by tilting the Nunchuk.

cards.heading: Split-screen combat returns with classic Bond characters
cards.text:
GoldenEye 007 features both offline split-screen for up to four local players and online play for up to eight players. There are 10 multiplayer maps. There are four different game modes for offline multiplayer and nine different game modes for online multiplayer. Online multiplayer is provided through the free Nintendo Wi-Fi Connection, and though up to eight players can connect to a game remotely, only one local player is allowed at a time.  Multiplayer includes characters from the single-player campaign, such as James Bond and Alec Trevelyan, as well as classic Bond-series characters including Jaws, Oddjob, and Julius No. Additionally, online multiplayer offers XP progression, unlockables and multipliers.

Split-screen combat provides over a dozen modifiers, including Melee Only, You Only Live Twice, and Paintball Mode from the original game.

cards.heading: David Arnold and Bruce Feirstein revisit the film
cards.text: David Arnold composed the score, while Nicole Scherzinger performs a new version of the title song originally sung by Tina Turner. Film co-writer Bruce Feirstein revised characters and events for the modern setting, including Trevelyan's background and a sequence at a Dubai arms fair.

main.title: Radiant Historia
main.subtitle: A soldier between possible histories
main.summary: Radiant Historia is Atlus and Headlock's Nintendo DS role-playing game about Stocke, a soldier on the war-torn continent of Vainqueur. The White Chronicle gives him a way to move between alternate histories as he seeks to prevent the land's desertification. A decision can lead to another branch of events, and returning with knowledge from elsewhere can make a different outcome possible. The adventure turns time travel into an ongoing responsibility. Stocke must learn which change is needed, then find the moment at which it can still be made.

cards.heading: A soldier between possible histories
cards.text: Radiant Historia is Atlus and Headlock's Nintendo DS role-playing game about Stocke, a soldier on the war-torn continent of Vainqueur. The White Chronicle gives him a way to move between alternate histories as he seeks to prevent the land's desertification. A decision can lead to another branch of events, and returning with knowledge from elsewhere can make a different outcome possible. The adventure turns time travel into an ongoing responsibility. Stocke must learn which change is needed, then find the moment at which it can still be made.

cards.heading: Arrange the enemy before the strike
cards.text: Battles use a grid on which enemies can be displaced and brought together. Attacks that move a target can set up a later blow against several opponents, making the order of actions important to the result. The player prepares a sequence rather than only choosing the strongest available command. This small spatial system gives ordinary encounters another layer of planning. A useful turn can begin by changing an enemy's position, allowing the next party member to exploit the arrangement that the first action has created.

cards.heading: Bring an answer from another path
cards.text: The world map connects self-contained locations that Stocke and his companions can investigate, while the Chronicle makes earlier decisions available for reconsideration. Information acquired along one branch can remove an obstacle in the other, so exploring both histories has a practical purpose. The structure gives a familiar role-playing journey a different sense of continuity: an apparent failure may identify what still needs to be learned. Radiant Historia connects its story about possible futures to a player who can revisit the past and act on an understanding earned elsewhere.

main.title: Kinect for Xbox 360
main.subtitle: When the Body Became the Controller
main.summary: Microsoft's Kinect uses cameras, microphones and body tracking to let Xbox 360 players interact without holding a gamepad.

cards.heading: The original Kinect sensor in 2010
cards.text: Microsoft launched Kinect for Xbox 360 in North America on November 4, 2010, followed by Europe on November 10 and Japan on November 20. Developed as Project Natal, it combines depth and video cameras, microphones and recognition software. Games such as Kinect Sports, Dance Central and Kinectimals turn movement in front of the television into play.

cards.heading: Using body movement to play
cards.text: Players can navigate menus with gestures, jump or run in place. Games must make those movements easy to recognise and show clearly when the sensor has understood them. The amount of room, distance from the television and physical effort become practical limits on what the controls can ask a player to do.

cards.heading: Recognising body parts and estimating joints
cards.text: Depth information helps the software distinguish a body from the background and estimate joint positions in real time. Microsoft Research used machine-learning methods trained on many poses to recognise different body shapes, clothes and movements. The tracking also had to leave enough Xbox 360 resources for the game itself.

cards.heading: Games and the physical play space
cards.text: The launch games use the sensor differently. Kinect Sports turns sporting gestures into competitions, Dance Central follows choreography, Kinectimals responds to movements around virtual pets and Your Shape: Fitness Evolved monitors exercise. Each needs to account for the player's position and the space available in front of the screen.

main.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops
main.subtitle: The War Inside a Memory
main.summary: Treyarch frames a Cold War campaign through Alex Mason's interrogation, alongside expanded multiplayer and cooperative Zombies.

cards.heading: A Cold War Call of Duty
cards.text: Call of Duty: Black Ops launched on November 9, 2010. Treyarch follows covert operations during the Cold War through the uncertain memories of Alex Mason. Competitive multiplayer adds COD Points, Wager Matches, Theater and Combat Training, while Zombies returns as a larger part of the package.

cards.heading: Mason under interrogation
cards.text: Alex Mason begins restrained in an interrogation room, questioned about past operations and a recurring sequence of numbers. Missions in Cuba, Vietnam and the Soviet Union unfold through his memories. The framing lets the campaign move between places and periods as the player tries to understand what Mason remembers.

cards.heading: COD Points, training and Theater
cards.text: Experience unlocks access to equipment, while COD Points provide a currency for choosing purchases. Wager Matches put that currency at risk. Combat Training offers practice against computer-controlled opponents, and Theater lets players revisit and study recorded matches. These tools add different ways to improve or compete between regular multiplayer rounds.

cards.heading: Returning to Zombies
cards.text: Four-player Zombies sends the group against increasingly difficult waves. Points buy weapons, open areas and operate equipment, while teammates must decide when to revive a fallen player or risk another purchase. Maps such as Kino der Toten add voices and secrets to the survival routine, encouraging players to investigate as well as endure.

main.title: Sonic Colors
main.subtitle: An interstellar amusement park
main.summary: Sonic Colors (known as Sonic Colours in PAL regions) is a 2010 platform game developed by Sonic Team and published by Sega.

cards.heading: An interstellar amusement park
cards.text: Sonic Colors (known as Sonic Colours in PAL regions) is a 2010 platform game developed by Sonic Team and published by Sega. It follows Sonic's quest to stop his nemesis Doctor Eggman from enslaving an alien race and taking over the world. The gameplay is similar to prior Sonic games, with players collecting rings and defeating enemies; the camera perspective often switches from third-person to side-scrolling perspectives. The game also introduces Wisps, power-ups the player can use to increase attack power and reach new areas.

cards.heading: The Wisps open new routes
cards.text: Eggman's Incredible Interstellar Amusement Park connects several planets, each hiding a power source Sonic must destroy. Rescued Wisps supply temporary abilities: Cyan Laser bounces from surfaces, Yellow Drill burrows through ground and water, Orange Rocket launches upward and Pink Spikes grips walls and ceilings. Other forms let Sonic hover along rings, change blocks or eat through obstacles. Their distinct uses open routes beyond straightforward running.

cards.heading: Balancing speed and platforming
cards.text: Development of Sonic Colors began following the completion of Sonic Unleashed in 2008, alongside Sonic Generations. While they kept most of Unleashed's core gameplay elements, developers Sonic Team and Dimps decided to create an equal balance between speed and platforming similar to that of the games released for the Sega Genesis, in comparison to the straightforward gameplay of Unleashed. Following requests by fans, the team also made the decision to make Sonic the only playable character, and to omit "gimmick" themes such as the swordplay mechanic used in the 2009 spin-off Sonic and the Black Knight. The team chose to develop Sonic Colors on Nintendo's Wii and DS consoles, hoping to expand upon the audience attracted by the successful Mario & Sonic at the Olympic Games crossover games.
